findings.issue_text: [BUG] The updated assertion `expect(datasource.applyTemplateVariables).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(5)` assumes one interpolation call per shard, but the diff moved interpolation into runShardSplitQuery before shard partitioning, so with a single target it is called once. With only one query in the request, applyTemplateVariables is invoked exactly once in runShardSplitQuery (the map over filtered targets) before splitQueriesByStreamShard runs, and splitQueriesByStreamShard (untouched by this diff) does not call applyTemplateVariables on the derived shard queries — so the assertion expects 5 calls and receives 1, making this test fail rather than pass.

[ADVISORY] The new map applies datasource.applyTemplateVariables in place over the request.targets objects, and the updated mocks in shardQuerySplitting.test.ts demonstrate the mutation pattern (query.expr = query.expr.replace(...)), so request.targets itself can be left with interpolated expressions. If the real applyTemplateVariables mutates like the mocks do, anything downstream that re-reads request.targets (e.g., query retry/secondary datasource flows that re-run the original request) sees already-interpolated expressions and any variable information is lost; previously interpolation happened via a separate call on the way in and the raw targets were still the canonical copy passed to runQuery consumers.

[ADVISORY] The new interpolation test in querySplitting.test.ts asserts only on the first runQuery call (mock.calls[0][0]), while runSplitQuery emits multiple split chunk requests whose targets are not asserted. A regression where only the first chunk is interpolated (or later chunks are re-derived from the raw uninterpolated target) would pass this test; the shard-side test has the same shape but at least verifies an interpolated shard-group query, leaving the split-path interpolation of chunks 2..N unverified.

[ADVISORY] Interpolation now happens before splitQueriesByStreamShard parses the expression for the stream selector, so the selector extraction now operates on interpolated text rather than the raw expression. Any template variable that expands into something the shard-splitting parser does not expect inside the selector (e.g., a variable expanding to a multi-value or containing a comma/brace) now changes which label values fetchLabelValues is called with, a code path only exercised by the happy-path selector variable in the tests; previously the parse operated on raw text when interpolation failed to resolve.

[BUG] runSplitQuery now interpolates every target (including range variables like $__auto) BEFORE partitioning with querySupportsSplitting, so splitting decisions are made on already-substituted expressions. If querySupportsSplitting/isLogsQuery-style detection keys on variable tokens ($__auto, $step, $__range) present in the raw expr, an interpolated expr no longer contains them, so queries that previously qualified for time-based splitting silently fall into the non-splitting path and execute as single unsplit requests — defeating the feature this module exists for. The added test only exercises the happy path where the mock replace() leaves a splittable shape.

[BUG] runSplitQuery previously performed no interpolation (it was deferred to the normal query pipeline downstream), and this diff adds it with no deduplication, so targets are interpolated here and then interpolated again by the downstream execution path. Variables with context-sensitive or stateful interpolation (scoped vars, multi-value with regex quoting, $__auto interval computed per intervalMs) get substituted twice, producing corrupted expressions (e.g. double-escaped label matchers) or losing the $__auto interval that downstream code needs to recompute per-chunk step sizes. The test masks this because datasource.runQuery is mocked, bypassing the real pipeline that also interpolates.

[ADVISORY] The filter(expr)/filter(!hide)/map(applyTemplateVariables) pipeline is now duplicated verbatim in querySplitting.ts and shardQuerySplitting.ts as hand-maintained parallel logic. The next change to how targets are prepared (e.g. adding a filter for adhoc filters, or reordering interpolation) must be applied in two places; this diff itself already shows the two files arriving at the same pipeline via different edits, and any drift between them yields queries that split differently depending on which splitter handles them.

[ADVISORY] applyTemplateVariables mutates the query object in place (the test mock at shardQuerySplitting.test.ts line 56-59 demonstrates the mutation contract: query.expr = query.expr.replace(...)), so the caller's request.targets objects are modified before splitting. runShardSplitQuery and runSplitQuery receive the caller's request; mutating targets means the original request object held by the panel/other consumers of the same request (retries, other data sources in a mixed datasource request) observes interpolated expressions, breaking any code that re-runs or introspects the original request with raw variables.

[ADVISORY] Filter order was inverted as part of this change (interpolate-then-filter became filter-then-interpolate) without any requirement in the stated intent requiring reordering. Hidden queries with empty/absent expr are now excluded before interpolation, which is fine, but any expr that becomes truthy or changes shape only after interpolation (e.g. expr set entirely from a template variable) is now evaluated on the raw value — a behavioral change smuggled into an API-swap commit that no test covers and that is untraceable to the stated 'interpolate before execution' intent.

[ADVISORY] The existing 'Interpolates queries before running' test now asserts applyTemplateVariables is called 5 times (once per shard-group query), entangling the test with an implementation detail that changed only as a side effect of the API swap. The call-count assertion pins the internal per-query interpolation strategy; a future refactor that batch-interpolates or caches interpolation breaks the test with no behavioral change, making safe refactoring of this path riskier than the behavior it protects warrants.

[BUG] Interpolation is applied BEFORE the split/non-split partition, so the $__auto marker that query splitting keys on is replaced (e.g. with a fixed '5m') before querySupportsSplitting/querySupportsSplitting sees the expression. Once applyTemplateVariables substitutes $__auto, a query that should be split into per-chunk range queries is classified as non-splitting (or split against a duration the splitter no longer controls), so long-range queries are sent as a single request — the exact behavior splitting exists to prevent. The new test masks this: it only asserts the interpolated expr/step and never asserts the chunk count, and its mock replaces $__auto with '5m' while the pre-existing '3 days, 3 chunks' tests rely on $__auto surviving to the splitter. Previously runSplitQuery did NOT interpolate, precisely so the splitter saw the raw marker.

[ADVISORY] The updated expectation asserts applyTemplateVariables is called 5 times for a single target, indicating interpolation now runs per shard group inside splitQueriesByStreamShard in addition to the explicit map in runShardSplitQuery — duplicated interpolation on the same query. Every shard-split request pays template interpolation cost multiple times per query, and any non-idempotent side effect in an applyTemplateVariables implementation (e.g. adhoc-filter application or filter appends) is applied repeatedly; next change to the interpolation pipeline has two call sites to keep in sync.

[ADVISORY] The test mocks for applyTemplateVariables mutate the input query object in place (query.expr = query.expr.replace(...)), matching an implementation style that mutates request.targets entries rather than returning copies. If the real LokiDatasource.applyTemplateVariables mutates the target, the raw uninterpolated expr on request.targets is destroyed before splitting logic runs, silently changing what any later consumer of request.targets sees; a cloning implementation and a mutating implementation are behaviorally different but the interface here does not distinguish them.

[BUG] runSplitQuery now interpolates via datasource.applyTemplateVariables, but the split results are then handed to datasource.runQuery, which interpolates targets again, so previously the splitting path never pre-interpolated — this changes the objective of the splitting path (from 'split raw targets' to 'split pre-interpolated targets') without any documented human acceptance of the double-interpolation semantics. Queries containing variable expressions that survive one interpolation pass (e.g. escaped $$var, or variables whose values themselves contain $-syntax) are interpolated twice, producing corrupted Loki queries or silently different results than the non-splitting path; users with such variables get wrong data on split queries only.

[BUG] applyTemplateVariables mutates the query object in place (the test mocks at shardQuerySplitting.test.ts lines 55-58 and 172-175 show the real contract: query.expr = query.expr.replace(...); return query), so the map call mutates the caller's request.targets entries, whereas the removed interpolateVariablesInQueries call returned fresh query objects. The original DataQueryRequest.targets are modified with interpolated expr values; any downstream consumer that re-runs or re-reads the original targets (e.g. query re-execution on refresh, panel repeat, or the non-splitting fallback path operating on the same request) sees mutated queries, and template variables can no longer be re-resolved on subsequent executions.

[BUG] The filter on query.expr now runs BEFORE interpolation, but the removed code interpolated first and then filtered, so queries whose expr consists solely of a variable that resolves to an empty string are no longer dropped. A dashboard variable that evaluates to empty (common pattern for optional filters) yields a target with expr '' that previously was filtered out and is now passed to splitQueriesByStreamShard/runQuery, producing failing or nonsensical Loki requests (stream-selector parse errors) where the old behavior silently skipped the query.

[ADVISORY] The swap from interpolateVariablesInQueries to per-query applyTemplateVariables silently changes which interpolation context is used (applyTemplateVariables receives request.filters as a third argument; the previous interpolateVariablesInQueries path did not pass filters), changing the objective without explicit acceptance. Queries in shard-split execution now resolve ad-hoc/filters-scoped variables differently than before; users relying on the previous filtering behavior get different query results with no changelog entry or test asserting the filters behavior.

[ADVISORY] The two splitting entry points now hand-maintain a duplicated filter/map pipeline (hide filter, expr filter, applyTemplateVariables map) in slightly different orders (querySplitting.ts filters hide before expr; shardQuerySplitting.ts filters expr before hide), which has already drifted once in this diff. The next change to target preprocessing must be replicated in both files in the correct order; a future edit to one path (e.g. adding instant-query handling) will silently diverge from the other, splitting behavior between splitting modes.

[ADVISORY] The updated 'Interpolates queries before running' test asserts `applyTemplateVariables` was called exactly 5 times, a magic number that mirrors the internal shard-grouping count rather than any contract. The count 5 is derived from fetchLabelValues returning 5 shard values grouped into shard groups; if the grouping algorithm changes shard-group cardinality without any change to interpolation behavior, this test breaks spuriously, and conversely a regression that drops a shard group can still pass as long as the count happens to be 5 — the assertion verifies implementation structure, not that every interpolated query reaches runQuery.

[ADVISORY] The mocked `applyTemplateVariables` mutates the query object in place and returns it, so the test passes regardless of whether the real `LokiDatasource.applyTemplateVariables` returns a fresh object; if the real implementation returns a new query, any code in `runShardSplitQuery` depending on in-place mutation would be untested. A future refactor of `applyTemplateVariables` to non-mutating semantics could break shard splitting while these mocks (also at lines 172-175 and querySplitting tests) silently keep the old contract, giving false confidence that the datasource's real template handling is compatible with the new per-query call site.

[ADVISORY] The new 'Interpolates queries before execution' test is duplicated nearly verbatim in shardQuerySplitting.test.ts (lines 84-101), two hand-maintained copies of the same mock `replace`/assertion setup. The next change to how interpolation is invoked (e.g. adding a fourth argument to `applyTemplateVariables`) must be replicated in both fixtures and the shared `createLokiDatasource` mock wiring; the copies will drift, as they already differ only in the shard-specific assertion, making one test's silent breakage easy to miss.

[BUG] The expr filter runs before applyTemplateVariables, so queries whose expr is entirely a template variable (e.g. expr: '$expr') are silently dropped from shard-split execution. A user whose panel builds the whole Loki expression from a dashboard variable gets no data and no error: the target is filtered out by .filter((query) => query.expr) before interpolation ever runs, whereas the old code called datasource.interpolateVariablesInQueries(request.targets, ...) first and then filtered, so such queries previously executed. Failure is invisible — an empty result presented as a successful query.

[BUG] runSplitQuery now interpolates targets via applyTemplateVariables before handing them to datasource.runQuery, which interpolates again, so variables are substituted twice on the splitting path. Expressions containing escaped or literal dollar sequences (e.g. a variable value that itself contains '$' or a '$__' macro that should survive to the backend) get re-processed on the second pass, producing a corrupted expr sent to Loki; previously this path passed raw targets to runQuery and interpolation happened exactly once. Wrong query results, not an error.

[ADVISORY] The diff removes the only call site of datasource.interpolateVariablesInQueries on this path without deprecating or migrating the public datasource method. Out-of-tree plugins or custom datasources that rely on the shard-splitting path going through interpolateVariablesInQueries (e.g. wrapping it for custom variable handling) silently stop being invoked — their hook becomes a no-op with no error surfaced, changing behavior on upgrade.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The expr filter runs before applyTemplateVariables, so queries whose expr is entirely a template variable (e.g. expr: '$expr') are silently dropped from shard-split execution. An expr that is entirely a template variable like `'$expr'` is still a non-empty string and therefore truthy, so it will NOT be filtered out before `applyTemplateVariables(...)` runs. The diff does change call order vs. the old `interpolateVariablesInQueries(...)`, but the specific claim that `expr: '$expr'` targets are “silently dropped” is not supported by the code shown.

Wrong query results, not an error.
